title: Tanzanian Oxtail Stew
community: Popular at Tanzanian restaurants and special occasions
author: Chef Jabir
desc: Tanzanian Oxtail Stew — oxtail slow-cooked for 2.5 hours in a rich spiced tomato and onion sauce until the meat falls from the bone and the sauce is gloriously thick and gelatinous. A restaurant favourite and a special occasion dish that rewards patience with extraordinary richness.
longDesc: Oxtail stew is Tanzania's most gelatinous, richest, and most patient meat dish. The 2.5-hour cook is non-negotiable — oxtail contains the most collagen of any beef cut, and only extended cooking converts it entirely to gelatin, producing the characteristic sticky, incredibly rich sauce.
steps: Add garlic, ginger, all spices, tomatoes. Cook 10 minutes until very thick.
Simmer covered on the lowest heat for 2—2.5 hours until meat falls from bone.
The sauce will be very thick and glossy.
chefTips: The longer the simmer the better — 3 hours is not too long.
Pressure cooker reduces time to 50—55 minutes.
The sauce should be so thick it coats the back of a spoon thickly.
cookingScience: Oxtail contains 40—50% collagen by dry weight — the highest of any beef cut. This makes it the richest source of gelatin when slow-cooked, producing the characteristically sticky, thick, naturally thickened sauce that cannot be replicated by any other cut.
sustainabilityTips: Oxtail uses a cut that would otherwise be undervalued.
culturalNote: Oxtail stew is Tanzania's most patient dish — a food that rewards those who are willing to wait. At Tanzanian restaurants, it is the dish that the serious meat-eater orders when they want the best.
